what: Classroom · timing variants with and without a sender frailty
title: Analyses of bundled event logs
text: Juozaitienė & Wit (2024) compare count statistics timing variants (time since recent reciprocating transitive event, continuous interrupted closing event). Count statistics also carry sender activity: actor sends lot accumulates large counts. Gamma sender frailty (random_effects = "sender") absorbs activity differences senders.  Without random effect count specification lowest AIC, ahead interrupted 423.2. sender frailty count specification still lowest AIC, lead interrupted 309.2. Among timing variants, interrupted fits better continuous 180.2 AIC points frailty model.
code: data(classroom_events) specs <- list(   count       = c("reciprocity_count", "transitivity_count"),   continuous  = c("reciprocity_time_recent", "transitivity_time_recent"),   interrupted = c("reciprocity_time_recent_interrupted",                   "transitivity_time_recent_interrupted"))  no_re <- compare_models(classroom_events, specs, n_controls = 3, seed = 11) no_re #>         model n_terms n_obs   log_lik      AIC delta_AIC #> 1       count       2   691 -653.3589 1310.718    0.0000 #> 2 interrupted       2   691 -864.9598 1733.920  423.2017 #> 3  continuous       2   691 -919.1762 1842.352  531.6345  with_re <- compare_models(classroom_events, specs, n_controls = 3, seed = 11,                           random_effects = "sender") with_re #>         model n_terms n_obs   log_lik      AIC delta_AIC #> 1       count       2   691 -525.3774 1092.430    0.0000 #> 2 interrupted       2   691 -679.7356 1401.603  309.1735 #> 3  continuous       2   691 -769.7646 1581.834  489.4043 cols <- c(count = "#d62728", continuous = "#2ca02c", interrupted = "#1f77b4") op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4, 4.5, 2.5, 1)) for (tab in list(no_re, with_re)) {   d <- setNames(tab$delta_AIC, tab$model)[names(specs)]   bp <- barplot(d, col = cols[names(d)], ylim = c(0, max(d) * 1.15),                 ylab = expression(Delta * "AIC"),                 main = if (identical(tab, no_re)) "no random effect" else "sender frailty")   text(bp, d, sprintf("%.1f", d), pos = 3, cex = 0.85) } par(op)

title: Analyses of bundled event logs
text: stratified Cox model pspline(stat, df = 4) four endogenous statistics, fitted first 30 days radoslaw_email dataset three controls per case. Statistics computed default endogenous_features() behaviour case-control data: controls scored history observed events without entering . time gap mapped recency weight transform_recency() (1 event just happened, falling towards 0 gap grows), dyad event gets weight 0.  panel shows one statistic’s contribution log-hazard, three held medians; band ±2 standard errors. fit two continuous variants rise steeply weight 0 (reciprocating transitive event yet) stay high, peaking recent events. interrupted reciprocity curve stays near zero large weights rises; interrupted transitivity curve highest weight 0 zero range.
code: data(radoslaw_email) re30 <- radoslaw_email[radoslaw_email$time < 30, ] re30 <- re30[re30$sender != re30$receiver, ]  stat_names <- c("reciprocity_time_recent",                 "transitivity_time_recent",                 "reciprocity_time_recent_interrupted",                 "transitivity_time_recent_interrupted")  cc   <- sample_non_events(re30, n_controls = 3, seed = 11) feat <- endogenous_features(cc, stats = stat_names) for (s in stat_names) {   w <- transform_recency(feat[[s]])   w[is.na(w)] <- 0                     # no such event yet: weight 0   feat[[s]] <- w }  library(survival)   # coxph() recognises pspline() and strata() only unqualified fit <- coxph(   Surv(rep(1, nrow(feat)), event) ~     pspline(reciprocity_time_recent,              df = 4) +     pspline(transitivity_time_recent,             df = 4) +     pspline(reciprocity_time_recent_interrupted,  df = 4) +     pspline(transitivity_time_recent_interrupted, df = 4) +     strata(stratum),   data = feat, method = "breslow") c(events = nrow(re30), actors = length(unique(c(re30$sender, re30$receiver)))) #> events actors  #>  10776    151 panel <- c("reciprocity · continuous", "transitivity · continuous",            "reciprocity · interrupted", "transitivity · interrupted") op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(4, 4.5, 2.5, 1)) for (j in seq_along(stat_names)) {   s <- stat_names[j]   rng <- stats::quantile(feat[[s]], c(0.02, 0.98))   nd <- feat[rep(1, 80), ]   for (o in stat_names) nd[[o]] <- stats::median(feat[[o]])   nd[[s]] <- seq(rng[1], rng[2], length.out = 80)   pr <- stats::predict(fit, newdata = nd, type = "terms", se.fit = TRUE)   k <- grep(s, colnames(pr$fit), fixed = TRUE)[1]   y <- pr$fit[, k]; se <- pr$se.fit[, k]   plot(nd[[s]], y, type = "n", ylim = range(y - 2 * se, y + 2 * se),        xlab = "recency weight", ylab = "partial log-hazard", main = panel[j])   polygon(c(nd[[s]], rev(nd[[s]])), c(y + 2 * se, rev(y - 2 * se)),           col = grDevices::adjustcolor("#1d4e89", 0.2), border = NA)   abline(h = 0, col = "grey60")   lines(nd[[s]], y, lwd = 2, col = "#1d4e89") } par(op)

text: events dyad-years: (government, opponent, year). events year share time, matters controls statistics. Risk set. question dyads fought active given year. sample_non_events(mode = "two") draw controls every government × opponent pair, pairs never fight (government rebel group another continent); dyad’s past separate events controls almost perfectly. controls therefore drawn dyads fought earlier year: five per event, uniformly, excluding event’s dyad. dyad’s first year (onset) comparable risk set left . control may dyad also fought year, another row: Breslow convention tied times, keeps tied event risk. Statistics. endogenous_features() updates history row row, event see rows year. use earlier years, year’s rows scored prior_log holding events earlier years empty history_log, row current year enters history.
code: ev <- u[order(u$year, u$dyad_id), ] el <- data.frame(sender = ev$sender, receiver = ev$receiver, time = ev$year) dk <- paste(el$sender, el$receiver, sep = "\r") first_year <- tapply(el$time, dk, min) set.seed(1) cc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(which(el$time > first_year[dk]), function(i) {   pool <- setdiff(names(first_year)[first_year < el$time[i]], dk[i])   sr <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(sample(pool, 5), "\r"))   data.frame(stratum = i, event = c(1L, rep(0L, 5)), sender = c(el$sender[i], sr[, 1]),              receiver = c(el$receiver[i], sr[, 2]), time = el$time[i]) })) c(strata = length(unique(cc$stratum)), rows = nrow(cc), onsets_left_out = sum(el$time == first_year[dk])) #>          strata            rows onsets_left_out  #>            2823           16938             695 yrs <- sort(unique(cc$time)) cc <- do.call(rbind, lapply(yrs, function(y)   endogenous_features(cc[cc$time == y, ], history_log = el[0, ],                       prior_log = if (any(el$time < y)) el[el$time < y, ],                       stats = c("recency", "sender_outdegree", "receiver_indegree")))) # the dyad's own past: number of earlier active years, and war last year dkey <- dk; ckey <- paste(cc$sender, cc$receiver, sep = "\r") cc$dyad_past <- mapply(function(k, t) sum(dkey == k & el$time < t), ckey, cc$time) war_key <- paste(dkey, el$time)[ev$intensity_level == 2] cc$war_last <- as.numeric(paste(ckey, cc$time - 1) %in% war_key) cc$last_year <- as.numeric(!is.na(cc$recency) & cc$recency == 1) # the government's other dyads active last year gov_last <- table(paste(el$sender, el$time)) cc$gov_other <- as.numeric(gov_last[paste(cc$sender, cc$time - 1)]); cc$gov_other[is.na(cc$gov_other)] <- 0 cc$gov_other <- cc$gov_other - cc$last_year cc$log_dyad_past <- log1p(cc$dyad_past) cc$log_gov_past <- log1p(cc$sender_outdegree); cc$log_opp_past <- log1p(cc$receiver_indegree) cc$log_gov_other <- log1p(cc$gov_other)

code: pairs <- aggregate(list(w = rep(1, nrow(flows))), flows[, c("s", "j")], sum) names(pairs) <- c("from", "to", "w") act <- table(c(flows$s, flows$j)) top <- names(sort(act, decreasing = TRUE))[1:150] strong <- pairs[pairs$from %in% top & pairs$to %in% top & pairs$w >= 5, ] g <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(strong[, c("from", "to")], directed = FALSE) main <- names(which(igraph::components(g)$membership == which.max(igraph::components(g)$csize))) strong <- strong[strong$from %in% main & strong$to %in% main, ] lay <- layout_graph(strong, ids = main, seed = 3) # bridging: share of a member's cosponsorships that go to the other party's bills as_cos <- flows[!is.na(flows$sp) & !is.na(flows$jp), ] bridge <- tapply(as_cos$sp != as_cos$jp, as_cos$j, mean) bridge_n <- table(as_cos$j) nodes <- data.frame(id = lay$id, x = lay$x, y = lay$y, size = as.numeric(act[lay$id]),                     col = party_col[party[lay$id]], label = NA) bridges <- names(sort(bridge[lay$id][bridge_n[lay$id] >= 50], decreasing = TRUE))[1:6] par(mar = c(0.5, 0.5, 3, 0.5)) draw_network(nodes, data.frame(from = strong$from, to = strong$to, w = strong$w,                                col = party_col[party[strong$from]]),              directed = TRUE, max_lwd = 2.4, ylim = c(-0.04, max(nodes$y) + 0.2)) # the bridging members: ringed, and labelled in a row above the graph with leader lines b_ <- nodes[nodes$id %in% bridges, ]; b_ <- b_[order(b_$x), ] points(b_$x, b_$y, pch = 21, bg = NA, col = ink, lwd = 2,        cex = 0.6 + 2.6 * sqrt(b_$size / max(nodes$size)) + 0.35) lx <- seq(0.1, 0.9, length.out = nrow(b_)); ly <- max(nodes$y) + c(0.09, 0.16)[seq_len(nrow(b_)) %% 2 + 1] segments(b_$x, b_$y, lx, ly - 0.012, col = ink, lwd = 0.7) text(lx, ly, short[b_$id], cex = 0.62, col = ink, pos = 3, offset = 0.15) title_left(sprintf("Cosponsorship among the %d most active members", nrow(lay)),            "arrow: sponsor to a member who cosponsored at least 5 of their bills; ringed and labelled: the six members whose cosponsorships most often cross party lines") legend_groups(setNames(party_col[c("D", "R")], party_name[c("D", "R")]), "bottomleft")

code: data(copenhagen_calls); data(copenhagen_sms); data(copenhagen_actors) calls <- copenhagen_calls[, c("sender", "receiver", "time", "duration")] sms   <- copenhagen_sms[,   c("sender", "receiver", "time")] fem   <- setNames(copenhagen_actors$female, copenhagen_actors$id)  pair <- function(d) paste(pmin(d$sender, d$receiver), pmax(d$sender, d$receiver)) pc <- table(pair(calls)); ps <- table(pair(sms)) both <- intersect(names(pc), names(ps)) data.frame(layer = c("calls", "text messages"),            events = c(nrow(calls), nrow(sms)),            students = c(length(unique(c(calls$sender, calls$receiver))),                         length(unique(c(sms$sender, sms$receiver)))),            pairs = c(length(pc), length(ps)),            pairs_in_both_layers = length(both)) #>           layer events students pairs pairs_in_both_layers #> 1         calls   3600      536   621                  438 #> 2 text messages  24333      568   697                  438 # one layout for both layers: the union of the two networks, largest component u <- rbind(data.frame(from = calls$sender, to = calls$receiver),            data.frame(from = sms$sender, to = sms$receiver)) u <- aggregate(list(w = rep(1, nrow(u))), u, sum) g <- igraph::graph_from_data_frame(u[, 1:2], directed = FALSE) comp <- igraph::components(g) giant <- names(comp$membership)[comp$membership == which.max(comp$csize)] lay <- layout_graph(u[u$from %in% giant & u$to %in% giant, ], ids = giant, seed = 3)  gcol <- c(female = pal[5], male = pal[4], unknown = "#B4BBC0") g_of <- function(id) ifelse(is.na(fem[id]), "unknown", ifelse(fem[id] == 1, "female", "male")) lcol <- c("calls and texts" = ink, "texts only" = pal[2], "calls only" = pal[6]) e <- data.frame(pair = union(names(pc), names(ps))) e$calls <- as.numeric(pc[e$pair]); e$texts <- as.numeric(ps[e$pair]) e$calls[is.na(e$calls)] <- 0; e$texts[is.na(e$texts)] <- 0 ab <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(e$pair, " ")); e$from <- ab[, 1]; e$to <- ab[, 2] e <- e[e$from %in% lay$id & e$to %in% lay$id, ] e$layer <- ifelse(e$calls > 0 & e$texts > 0, "calls and texts", ifelse(e$texts > 0, "texts only", "calls only")) e$w <- pmax(e$calls + e$texts, 4); e$col <- lcol[e$layer]   # pairs with 4 or fewer events share the thinnest visible line act <- table(c(calls$sender, calls$receiver, sms$sender, sms$receiver)) nodes <- data.frame(id = lay$id, x = lay$x, y = lay$y, size = as.numeric(act[lay$id]),                     col = gcol[g_of(lay$id)]) # a pair is "peripheral" when one of its students has no other partner in either layer deg <- table(c(e$from, e$to)) e$leaf <- deg[e$from] == 1 | deg[e$to] == 1 nodes$col <- "#8C969D" op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3), mar = c(0.1, 0.1, 3.2, 0.1), oma = c(0, 0, 2, 0)) for (L in names(lcol)) {   k <- e$layer == L   # draw_network scales widths to the panel's largest pair; rescale so all panels share one scale   ml <- 3.4 * (log1p(max(e$w[k])) / log1p(max(e$w)))^1.4   bg <- e[, c("from", "to")]; bg$w <- 1; bg$col <- "#DCE0E3"      # the whole network, faint, behind each panel   draw_network(transform(nodes, col = "#E6E9EB"), bg, directed = FALSE, max_lwd = 0.4,                node_scale = c(0.35, 1.8), xlim = c(-0.02, 1.02), ylim = c(-0.02, max(nodes$y) + 0.02))   draw_network(nodes[nodes$id %in% c(e$from[k], e$to[k]), ], e[k, c("from", "to", "w", "col")],                directed = FALSE, max_lwd = ml, node_scale = c(0.35, 1.8), add = TRUE)   title_left(sprintf("%s: %s pairs", L, fmt(sum(k))),              sprintf("%s end at a student with no other partner", pct(mean(e$leaf[k]), 0))) } mtext("All three kinds of pair run through the same network", side = 3, outer = TRUE, line = 0.5, adj = 0.01, cex = 0.95, font = 2, col = ink) mtext(sprintf("Same %s students at the same positions in every panel; grey: the whole network; line width: calls + texts, one scale for all panels",               fmt(length(giant))), side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = -1.2, cex = 0.68, col = ink_soft) par(op) nl <- table(factor(e$layer, levels = names(lcol))) leaf_share <- tapply(e$leaf, factor(e$layer, levels = names(lcol)), mean) pairs <- union(names(pc), names(ps)) n_call <- as.numeric(pc[pairs]); n_call[is.na(n_call)] <- 0 n_sms  <- as.numeric(ps[pairs]); n_sms[is.na(n_sms)] <- 0 ends <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(pairs, " ")) comp_g <- ifelse(is.na(fem[ends[, 1]]) | is.na(fem[ends[, 2]]), "unknown",           ifelse(fem[ends[, 1]] == fem[ends[, 2]], "same gender", "mixed gender")) ccol <- c("same gender" = pal[1], "mixed gender" = pal[6], unknown = "#B4BBC0") set.seed(4) jit <- function(n) runif(length(n), -0.12, 0.12) # every integer column and row gets the same small jitter x <- log10(n_call + 1) + runif(length(n_call), -0.035, 0.035) + ifelse(n_call == 0, jit(n_call), 0) y <- log10(n_sms + 1)  + runif(length(n_sms), -0.035, 0.035) + ifelse(n_sms == 0, jit(n_sms), 0) par(mar = c(4, 4.4, 2.8, 4)) plot(x, y, pch = 21, bg = alpha(ccol[comp_g], 0.55), col = "white", cex = 1.1, lwd = 0.4,      axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", xlim = c(-0.15, max(x) + 0.1), ylim = c(-0.15, max(y) + 0.1)) at <- c(0, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000) axis(1, at = log10(at + 1), labels = at, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5) axis(2, at = log10(at + 1), labels = at, las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5) mtext("calls between the pair", side = 1, line = 2, cex = 0.8, col = ink_soft) mtext("text messages between the pair", side = 2, line = 2.6, cex = 0.8, col = ink_soft) abline(h = 0.17, v = 0.17, col = rule, lty = 3) r_both <- cor(log1p(n_call[n_call > 0 & n_sms > 0]), log1p(n_sms[n_call > 0 & n_sms > 0])) # median texts per bin of calls, pairs using both channels bb <- n_call > 0 & n_sms > 0; br <- c(1, 2, 3, 5, 9, 17, 33, 200) bin <- cut(n_call[bb], br, right = FALSE) med <- tapply(log10(n_sms[bb] + 1), bin, median); mx <- tapply(log10(n_call[bb] + 1), bin, median) lines(mx, med, col = ink, lwd = 2.2); points(mx, med, pch = 21, bg = ink, col = "white", cex = 1.1) text(mx[length(mx)], med[length(med)], "median texts\nper calls bin", pos = 4, cex = 0.65, col = ink, xpd = TRUE) title_left("Pairs that call also text",            sprintf("n = %s pairs: %s both, %s only text, %s only call (on the axes); code: # number of events of pair (s -> r) in `log` strictly before each query time past_count <- function(s, r, t, log) {   q <- data.frame(k = paste(s, r), t = t, is_log = 0L, id = seq_along(t))   l <- data.frame(k = paste(log$sender, log$receiver), t = log$time, is_log = 1L, id = NA)   a <- rbind(q, l)   a <- a[order(a$k, a$t, a$is_log), ]          # at equal times the query comes first   before <- ave(a$is_log, a$k, FUN = cumsum)   out <- integer(length(t)); out[a$id[a$is_log == 0L]] <- before[a$is_log == 0L]   out } add_stats <- function(cc, own, other) {   cc <- endogenous_features(cc, stats = c("reciprocity_count", "sender_outdegree",                                           "receiver_indegree"), history_log = own)   cc$repetition   <- past_count(cc$sender, cc$receiver, cc$time, own)   cc$cross_same   <- past_count(cc$sender, cc$receiver, cc$time, other)   cc$cross_rev    <- past_count(cc$receiver, cc$sender, cc$time, other)   for (v in c("repetition", "reciprocity_count", "sender_outdegree", "receiver_indegree",               "cross_same", "cross_rev")) {     x <- cc[[v]]; x[is.na(x)] <- 0; cc[[paste0("l_", v)]] <- log1p(x)   }   gs <- fem[cc$sender]; gr <- fem[cc$receiver]   cc$gender_unknown <- as.integer(is.na(gs) | is.na(gr))   cc$same_gender    <- as.integer(!is.na(gs) & !is.na(gr) & gs == gr)   cc } cc_call <- add_stats(cc_call, own = calls, other = sms) cc_sms  <- add_stats(cc_sms,  own = sms,   other = calls) round(rbind(   calls = tapply(cc_call$cross_same > 0, cc_call$event, mean),   texts = tapply(cc_sms$cross_same > 0, cc_sms$event, mean)), 3)   # share with past contact in the other layer: controls (0), events (1) #>           0     1 #> calls 0.003 0.761 #> texts 0.002 0.583

fac <- fac[log(fac) >= par("usr")[1] & log(fac) <= par("usr")[2]]   axis(1, at = log(fac), labels = paste0("\u00d7", fac), tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.78, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5)   axis(2, at = y, labels = labels, las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.78, col.axis = ink, line = -0.6)   mtext("rate ratio: one earlier event against none (counts), or the pair having the attribute",         side = 1, line = 2.2, cex = 0.72, col = ink_soft)   legend("bottomright", legend = c("interval excludes \u00d71", "interval includes \u00d71"), pch = 21,          pt.bg = c(ink_soft, "white"), col = ink_soft, pt.cex = 1.4, bty = "n", cex = 0.75, text.col = ink) } forest2(list(calls = fit_call, `text messages` = fit_sms), pal[1:2], labels) title_left("What raises the rate of a call and of a text message",            "conditional logistic models, one per layer, same statistics; dh_s <- smooth_data(g_sms$fit, 1) yl <- range(dh_c$fit - 1.96 * dh_c$se, dh_c$fit + 1.96 * dh_c$se, dh_s$fit - 1.96 * dh_s$se, dh_s$fit + 1.96 * dh_s$se) par(mar = c(3.6, 4.2, 3, 7)) band <- function(d, col) {   lo <- d$fit - 1.96 * d$se; hi <- d$fit + 1.96 * d$se   polygon(c(d$x, rev(d$x)), c(lo, rev(hi)), col = alpha(col, 0.12), border = NA)   lines(d$x, lo, col = alpha(col, 0.6), lwd = 0.8, lty = 3); lines(d$x, hi, col = alpha(col, 0.6), lwd = 0.8, lty = 3) } plot(dh_c$x, dh_c$fit, type = "n", ylim = yl, axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "", xlim = c(0, 24)) abline(h = 0, col = rule, lwd = 1.2) band(dh_c, pal[1]); band(dh_s, pal[2]) lines(dh_c$x, dh_c$fit, col = pal[1], lwd = 2.4); lines(dh_s$x, dh_s$fit, col = pal[2], lwd = 2.4) axis(1, at = seq(0, 24, 3), labels = sprintf("%02d:00", seq(0, 24, 3)), tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5) axis(2, las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5) mtext("time of day, if the study day starts at midnight", side = 1, line = 2, cex = 0.75, col = ink_soft) mtext("effect on the log-rate", side = 2, line = 2.3, cex = 0.75, col = ink_soft) n <- nrow(dh_c) text(24, dh_c$fit[n] - 0.08, "calls", pos = 4, col = pal[1], cex = 0.8, xpd = TRUE) text(24, dh_s$fit[n] + 0.08, "text messages", pos = 4, col = pal[2], cex = 0.8, xpd = TRUE) # trough-to-peak bracket for calls xt <- dh_c$x[which.min(dh_c$fit)]; xp <- dh_c$x[which.max(dh_c$fit)] arrows(xp + 1.6, min(dh_c$fit), xp + 1.6, max(dh_c$fit), code = 3, length = 0.05, angle = 90, col = ink, lwd = 1) segments(xt, min(dh_c$fit), xp + 1.6, min(dh_c$fit), col = alpha(ink, 0.35), lty = 2) text(xp + 1.9, mean(range(dh_c$fit)), sprintf("peak / trough:\n%s\u00d7 for calls\n%s\u00d7 for texts", fmt(exp(diff(range(dh_c$fit))), 0), fmt(exp(diff(range(dh_s$fit))), 0)),      adj = 0, cex = 0.68, col = ink, xpd = TRUE) title_left("A similar daily cycle in both channels",            "effect of the time of day on the log-rate (cyclic smooth, dotted lines: 95% band), next to the history terms")

text: model matches 1990–2019 (26,282 matches). match, sample_non_events() draws one pair teams played (scope = "appearance"); run whole record since 1872 “played ” counts every earlier match, 1990–2019 strata kept. sampler draws ordered pairs; control put alphabetical order matches. endogenous_features() computes directed statistics, undirected ones computed match history strictly row’s time, previous ten years: activity: matches played two teams; common opponents: teams played (triadic closure); repetition: earlier matches two teams; years since last meeting, time since 1872, indicator pairs never met. regional groups model found 1960–1989 matches, grouping use matches meant explain. Teams play (many post-1990 states among ) belong group.  Pairs meet within days, two legs tie two matches one tournament, highest rate. Holding terms fixed, pairing whose last meeting one year ago log-rate 0.94 higher one last met ten years ago (factor 2.6). Common opponents carry largest linear effect, 1.80 per unit log(1 + common opponents) (s.e. 0.04); pair 1960–1989 group log-rate 0.45 higher (s.e. 0.05). Activity enters -0.36: given common opponents, grow activity, active teams meet .
code: hist <- f[f$t < 2020, c("a", "b", "t", "tournament")] hist <- hist[order(hist$t), ] cc <- sample_non_events(data.frame(sender = hist$a, receiver = hist$b, time = hist$t),                         scope = "appearance", seed = 1) cc <- cc[cc$time >= 1990, ] swap <- cc$sender > cc$receiver cc[swap, c("sender", "receiver")] <- cc[swap, c("receiver", "sender")] table(cc$event) #>  #>     0     1  #> 26282 26282 und_stats <- function(i, j, t, hist, window = 10) {   team <- c(hist$a, hist$b); opp <- c(hist$b, hist$a); tt <- c(hist$t, hist$t)   o <- order(team, tt); team <- team[o]; opp <- opp[o]; tt <- tt[o]   first <- match(unique(team), team); names(first) <- unique(team)   last <- c(first[-1] - 1, length(team)); names(last) <- names(first)   pt <- split(hist$t, paste(hist$a, hist$b, sep = "|"))   recent <- function(x, s) {       # matches of team x in [s - window, s)     if (is.na(first[x])) return(list(n = 0, opp = character(0)))     r <- first[x]:last[x]; tx <- tt[r]     hi <- findInterval(s, tx, left.open = TRUE); lo <- findInterval(s - window, tx, left.open = TRUE)     k <- if (hi > lo) r[(lo + 1):hi] else integer(0)     list(n = length(k), opp = unique(opp[k]))   }   out <- t(vapply(seq_along(i), function(k) {     a <- recent(i[k], t[k]); b <- recent(j[k], t[k])     p <- pt[[paste(i[k], j[k], sep = "|")]]; p <- p[p < t[k]]     c(act_i = a$n, act_j = b$n, common = length(intersect(a$opp, b$opp)),       pair = sum(p >= t[k] - window), since = if (length(p)) t[k] - max(p) else NA)   }, numeric(5)))   as.data.frame(out) } cc <- cbind(cc, und_stats(cc$sender, cc$receiver, cc$time, hist)) old <- f[f$t >= 1960 & f$t < 1990, ] old_pairs <- aggregate(list(w = rep(1, nrow(old))), list(from = old$a, to = old$b), sum) g_old <- layout_graph(old_pairs) grp <- setNames(g_old$group, g_old$id) cc$same_group <- as.integer(!is.na(grp[cc$sender]) & !is.na(grp[cc$receiver]) &                             grp[cc$sender] == grp[cc$receiver]) cc$never <- as.integer(is.na(cc$since)) cc$log_since <- log(ifelse(is.na(cc$since), max(cc$since, na.rm = TRUE), cc$since)) cc$log_activity <- log1p(cc$act_i) + log1p(cc$act_j) cc$log_common <- log1p(cc$common) cc$log_pair <- log1p(cc$pair) aggregate(cbind(act_i, common, pair, never) ~ event, cc, mean) #>   event    act_i    common      pair     never #> 1     0 58.30538  3.075527 0.2207975 0.8722319 #> 2     1 88.36725 17.334411 2.7739518 0.1584735 cv <- c("log_activity", "log_common", "log_pair", "same_group", "never", "log_since") w <- widen_case_control(cc, covariates = cv) fit <- rem(~ log_activity + log_common + log_pair + same_group + never + nl(log_since, k = 6),            data = w, method = "gam") est <- summary(fit)$p.table[, c("Estimate", "Std. Error")] round(est, 3) #>              Estimate Std. Error #> log_activity   -0.357      0.018 #> log_common      1.801      0.040 #> log_pair        0.189      0.068 #> same_group      0.446      0.051 #> never          -0.281      0.287 d <- smooth_data(fit$fit, 1)                      # x is log(years) lo <- d$fit - 1.96 * d$se; hi <- d$fit + 1.96 * d$se par(mar = c(3.4, 3.8, 2.6, 1)) plot(d$x, d$fit, type = "n", ylim = range(lo, hi, 0), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "") abline(h = 0, col = rule, lwd = 1.2) polygon(c(d$x, rev(d$x)), c(lo, rev(hi)), col = alpha(pal[1], 0.18), border = NA) lines(d$x, d$fit, col = pal[1], lwd = 2.2) yrs <- c(1 / 52, 1 / 12, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100) yrs <- yrs[log(yrs) >= min(d$x) & log(yrs) <= max(d$x)] axis(1, at = log(yrs), labels = c("1 week", "1 month", "6 months", "1", "2", "5", "10", "20", "50", "100")[   match(yrs, c(1 / 52, 1 / 12, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100))], tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5) axis(2, las = 1, tick = FALSE, cex.axis = 0.75, col.axis = ink_soft, line = -0.5) mtext("years since the two teams last met (log scale)", side = 1, line = 2, cex = 0.75, col = ink_soft) mtext("effect on the log-rate", side = 2, line = 2.3, cex = 0.75, col = ink_soft) y1 <- d$fit[which.min(abs(d$x - log(1)))]; y10 <- d$fit[which.min(abs(d$x - log(10)))] points(log(c(1, 10)), c(y1, y10), pch = 21, bg = "white", col = ink, cex = 1.2, lwd = 1.4) segments(log(1), y1, log(10), y1, col = ink_soft, lty = 3); segments(log(10), y1, log(10), y10, col = ink_soft, lty = 3) text(mean(log(c(1, 10))), y1 + 0.45, sprintf("1 year vs 10 years: %s times the rate", fmt(exp(y1 - y10), 1)), cex = 0.7, col = ink) title_left("A pairing is most likely soon after the last meeting",            "smooth effect of the time since the last meeting, with 95% band; other terms held fixed")

title: Endogenous mechanisms and time-varying global covariates
text: reciprocity_count built-endogenous statistic: value statistic candidate dyad (s, r) number past events (r, s). positive coefficient means event raises future rate reverse dyad. Recover coefficient one-parameter conditional logit fit within-stratum statistic difference: estimate sits ballpark simulated true_beta = 0.6.
code: set.seed(2024) actors <- as.character(1:10) true_beta <- 0.6  cc <- simulate_relational_events(   n_events = 1200,   senders = actors,   receivers = actors,   baseline_rate = 1,   allow_loops = FALSE,   n_controls = 1,   endogenous_stats = "reciprocity_count",   endogenous_effects = true_beta ) head(cc) #>   stratum event sender receiver        time reciprocity_count #> 1       1     1     10        3 0.007487612                 0 #> 2       1     0      1        6 0.007487612                 0 #> 3       2     1      2        5 0.011851596                 0 #> 4       2     0      9        2 0.011851596                 0 #> 5       3     1      8        3 0.026647847                 0 #> 6       3     0      3        4 0.026647847                 0 library(mgcv) cases    <- cc[cc$event == 1L, ] controls <- cc[cc$event == 0L, ] cases    <- cases[order(cases$stratum), ] controls <- controls[order(controls$stratum), ] fit_df <- data.frame(   one     = 1,   delta_r = cases$reciprocity_count - controls$reciprocity_count ) fit <- gam(one ~ delta_r - 1, family = "binomial", data = fit_df) unname(coef(fit)[1]) #> [1] 0.4563272

title: Endogenous mechanisms and time-varying global covariates

code: m <- c(reciprocity_count  = "linear",        transitivity_count = "linear")  gu_r <- gof_univariate(classroom_events, m, "reciprocity_count",  seed = 11) gu_t <- gof_univariate(classroom_events, m, "transitivity_count", seed = 11) gg   <- gof_global(classroom_events, m, seed = 11)  rbind(reciprocity_count  = c(statistic = gu_r$statistic, p_value = gu_r$p_value),       transitivity_count = c(statistic = gu_t$statistic, p_value = gu_t$p_value),       global             = c(statistic = gg$statistic,   p_value = gg$p_value)) #>                    statistic    p_value #> reciprocity_count  0.7514555 0.62471719 #> transitivity_count 1.2504243 0.08768022 #> global             1.5624453 0.18122308 # 95% pointwise envelope of |Brownian bridge| by simulation set.seed(99) u <- gu_r$u; n_grid <- length(u) env <- replicate(500, {   b <- cumsum(rnorm(n_grid, sd = sqrt(1 / n_grid)))   abs(b - u * b[n_grid]) }) band <- apply(env, 1, stats::quantile, 0.95) plot(u, abs(gu_r$W), type = "n", ylim = c(0, 1.35 * max(abs(c(gu_r$W, gu_t$W)), band)),      xlab = "u (rescaled event index)", ylab = expression("|" * hat(W)(u) * "|")) polygon(c(u, rev(u)), c(band, rep(0, n_grid)), col = "grey85", border = NA) lines(gu_r$u, abs(gu_r$W), lwd = 2, col = "#1d4e89") lines(gu_t$u, abs(gu_t$W), lwd = 2, col = "#d97706") legend("top", bty = "n", lwd = 2, col = c("#1d4e89", "#d97706"), horiz = TRUE, cex = 0.85,        legend = sprintf("%s (p = %.3f)", c("reciprocity_count", "transitivity_count"),                         c(gu_r$p_value, gu_t$p_value)))

code: set.seed(7) p <- 15; n <- 800 d <- matrix(runif(p * p, 0, 6), p, p); diag(d) <- NA ids <- which(!is.na(d)) f <- function(x) sin(x) - 0.3 * (x - 3)            # true effect ev <- sample(ids, n, replace = TRUE, prob = exp(f(d[ids]))) nv <- vapply(ev, function(e) sample(ids[ids != e], 1), 0) w <- data.frame(time = seq_len(n), x_ev = d[ev], x_nv = d[nv]) w$x <- w$x_ev - w$x_nv  fit_lin <- rem(~ x,     data = w, method = "gam", time = "time") fit_nl  <- rem(~ nl(x), data = w, method = "gam", time = "time") g_lin <- gof_rem(fit_lin, "x", test = "functional_form", data = w, seed = 1) g_nl  <- gof_rem(fit_nl,  "x", test = "functional_form", seed = 1) g_lin #> Martingale-residual GoF test of 'x': functional form #>   sup statistic = 1.0411, p-value = 0.0000 (2000 bootstrap replicates, n = 800) g_nl #> Martingale-residual GoF test of 'x': functional form #>   sup statistic = 0.2041, p-value = 0.6535 (2000 bootstrap replicates, n = 800) op <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) plot(g_lin, main = "linear fit"); plot(g_nl, main = "nl() fit") par(op)

what: Recovering the effect with a GAM
title: Exogenous dyadic covariates
text: event–control pair compute difference log-distance. GAM smooth term s(delta_dist) recover true curve.
code: library(mgcv) #> Loading required package: nlme #> This is mgcv 1.9-4. For overview type '?mgcv'.  get_dist <- function(s, r) {     dist_log[cbind(match(s, states), match(r, states))] }  events$dist_val <- mapply(get_dist, events$sender, events$receiver)  cases <- events[events$event == 1, ] controls <- events[events$event == 0, ] cases <- cases[order(cases$stratum), ] controls <- controls[order(controls$stratum), ]  fit_df <- data.frame(     y          = 1,     delta_dist = cases$dist_val - controls$dist_val )  fit <- gam(y ~ s(delta_dist) - 1, family = binomial, data = fit_df) summary(fit) #>  #> Family: binomial  #> Link function: logit  #>  #> Formula: #> y ~ s(delta_dist) - 1 #>  #> Approximate significance of smooth terms: #>               edf Ref.df Chi.sq p-value #> s(delta_dist)   1      1      0       1 #>  #> R-sq.(adj) =   -Inf   Deviance explained = -Inf% #> UBRE = 0.38879  Scale est. = 1         n = 800

title: Hyperedge models
text: amorem supports relational hyper event models (RHEMs), extension REMs dyadic (sender, receiver, time) events set-valued (, J, time) hyperedges, set senders J set receivers. Following Boschi, Lerner & Wit (2025), single event can involve several actors per axis: paper authored co-author set citing set references, e-mail sent several recipients , multi-actor meeting (J = ∅). code page runs page built.

title: Hyperedge models

Grouping rows sender time gives directed hyperevent: = {sender}, J = {recipients}. use first 7 days.  1,808 e-mails, 248 (14%) one recipient; account 44% 2,794 rows dyadic log. largest recipient set 135 members. figure draws multi-recipient e-mails busiest hour; week, 54% recipients multi-recipient e-mails belong sender’s group e-mail network. animation steps week 3-hour windows Warsaw time. busiest window, Wed 06 Jan 09:00–12:00, holds 25 248 multi-recipient e-mails, 24 49 windows none. single-recipient e-mails form ordinary dyadic log , dyadic catalogue applies directly:

title: Hyperedge models
text: amorem yet sample non-events hyperevents, case-control design built hand: e-mail, one control hyperedge number recipients, sender drawn uniformly actors recipient set drawn uniformly actors (matching cardinality, Section 3.3 paper). Three statistics evaluated event control event’s time, e-mails strictly : sender activity: past e-mails sender (hyperedge_subrep(rho = 1, l = 0)); repetition: past e-mails sender recipient, averaged recipients (hyperedge_subrep(rho = 1, l = 1)); reciprocity: past e-mails recipient sender, averaged recipients (hyperedge_activity() roles swapped).  three statistics enter log(1 + count) scale. Holding two fixed, log-rate e-mail changes 0.55 (standard error 0.08) per unit sender activity, 1.34 (s.e. 0.25) per unit repetition 4.38 (s.e. 0.32) per unit reciprocity. control drawn actor sets size, coefficients compare e-mail arbitrary hyperedge size; design also matches sender isolate recipient-side effects.
code: hstats <- function(I, J, t) c(   sender_activity = hyperedge_subrep(email_hl, I, J, t, rho = 1, l = 0),   repetition      = hyperedge_subrep(email_hl, I, J, t, rho = 1, l = 1),   reciprocity     = mean(vapply(J, function(j)                       hyperedge_activity(email_hl, I = j, J = I, t = t), 0)))  set.seed(11) actors <- sort(unique(c(unlist(email_hl$I), unlist(email_hl$J)))) rows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(email_hl)), function(i) {   I <- email_hl$I[[i]]; J <- email_hl$J[[i]]; t <- email_hl$time[i]   s_c <- sample(actors, 1)   J_c <- sample(setdiff(actors, s_c), length(J))   rbind(data.frame(stratum = i, event = 1L, t(hstats(I, J, t))),         data.frame(stratum = i, event = 0L, t(hstats(s_c, J_c, t)))) }) cc <- do.call(rbind, rows) for (v in c("sender_activity", "repetition", "reciprocity"))   cc[[paste0("log_", v)]] <- log1p(cc[[v]])  w <- widen_case_control(cc, covariates = c("log_sender_activity",                                            "log_repetition", "log_reciprocity")) fit <- rem(~ log_sender_activity + log_repetition + log_reciprocity,            data = w, method = "gam") est <- summary(fit)$p.table[, c("Estimate", "Std. Error")] round(est, 3) #>                     Estimate Std. Error #> log_sender_activity    0.551      0.081 #> log_repetition         1.344      0.254 #> log_reciprocity        4.377      0.323

title: Hyperedge models
text: citation-style data (Boschi et al. 2025 Section 5), simulate_directed_hyperedge_events() draws sender receiver sets two actor pools. Supported endogenous statistics: "size_I", "size_J", "activity", "subrep_<rho>_<l>". 150-event sweep 4 senders × 4 receivers, varying endogenous terms one time:  panel shows 150 events one simulation, one column per event: teal marks senders (authors A1–A4), purple marks receivers (papers P1–P4, shaded band), number teal marks column sender-set size. subrep_1_1 = 0.8 every event event 39 repeats sender receiver sets; effects, every event event 18 . endogenous effect, 30% events single sender. negative size_I effect raises share 47%; positive subrep_1_1 effect raises 85%, since reinforces sender-receiver pairs already occurred; effects together give 95%. simulator enumerates every candidate (, J) every event, cost per event grows exponentially actor pools; practical small universes (10 actors per side, max_size ≤ 3).
code: specs <- list(   "no effect"         = c(),   "size_I = -0.6"     = c(size_I = -0.6),   "subrep_1_1 = 0.8"  = c(subrep_1_1 = 0.8),   "both"              = c(size_I = -0.6, subrep_1_1 = 0.8)) sims <- lapply(specs, function(eff) {   set.seed(2)   simulate_directed_hyperedge_events(     n_events = 150, senders = paste0("author", 1:4),     receivers = paste0("paper", 1:4), max_size_I = 3, max_size_J = 3,     baseline_rate = 0.3,     endogenous_stats = if (length(eff)) names(eff) else NULL,     endogenous_effects = if (length(eff)) eff else NULL) }) sizes <- lapply(sims, hyperedge_sizes) sweep <- data.frame(   mean_size_I = vapply(sizes, function(s) mean(s$size_I), 0),   mean_size_J = vapply(sizes, function(s) mean(s$size_J), 0),   share_I_1   = vapply(sizes, function(s) mean(s$size_I == 1), 0)) round(sweep, 2) #>                  mean_size_I mean_size_J share_I_1 #> no effect               2.02        1.91      0.30 #> size_I = -0.6           1.71        2.07      0.47 #> subrep_1_1 = 0.8        1.19        1.14      0.85 #> both                    1.07        1.10      0.95

title: Model comparison on a real REM dataset
text: compare_models() accepts named list character vectors. entry one candidate specification; vector contents endogenous statistic names. compare three minimal specifications: paper’s definitions r(1c)/t(1c) (count), r(4ac)/t(7ac) (continuous timing), r(4ai)/t(7ai) (interrupted timing).

title: Model comparison on a real REM dataset
text: helper draws one case-control sample (default n_controls = 1) shared across every specification, computes union requested statistics endogenous_features(), builds case-minus-control differences, fits one -intercept binomial GLM per spec. Returned rows sorted AIC; winning spec delta_AIC = 0. Classroom count-based specification wins stripped-comparison — recall -smooth, -random-effect baseline; richer fits (thin-plate splines differences, sender/receiver random effects) typically reweight ranking favour temporal definitions, matching empirical findings paper.

title: Model comparison on a real REM dataset
text: compare_models() returns AIC summaries. inspect coefficients single spec, build case-control sample fit directly: recipe scales subset statistics catalogue. Use ?endogenous_features see full list.
code: stat_set <- specs$interrupted cc <- sample_non_events(classroom_events, n_controls = 1,                         scope = "all", mode = "one", seed = 11) cc_feat <- endogenous_features(cc, stats = stat_set) for (st in stat_set) cc_feat[[st]][is.na(cc_feat[[st]])] <- 0  cases <- cc_feat[cc_feat$event == 1L, ] ctrls <- cc_feat[cc_feat$event == 0L, ] cases <- cases[order(cases$stratum), ] ctrls <- ctrls[order(ctrls$stratum), ]  df <- data.frame(   one      = rep(1, nrow(cases)),   d_rec    = cases[[stat_set[1]]] - ctrls[[stat_set[1]]],   d_trans  = cases[[stat_set[2]]] - ctrls[[stat_set[2]]])  fit <- glm(one ~ d_rec + d_trans - 1, family = "binomial", data = df) summary(fit)$coefficients #>            Estimate Std. title: Quick start

title: Quick start
text: 20-actor network, 1200 events, single endogenous mechanism — reciprocity strength β = 0.6: 95% interval (0.35, 0.73) covers true coefficient 0.6. simulator emits case-control table directly (one sampled non-event per event n_controls = 1), recovery step single clogit call. preprocessed case-control data (e.g. eventnet) fit, case-1-control degenerate-logistic variant, smooth (TV / NL / TVNL) effects available one interface, rem() — see Estimation.
code: library(amorem) suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(survival))  set.seed(1) cc <- simulate_relational_events(   n_events           = 1200,   senders            = paste0("a", 1:20),   receivers          = paste0("a", 1:20),   baseline_rate      = 1,   n_controls         = 1,                 # one matched non-event per event   endogenous_stats   = "reciprocity_count",   endogenous_effects = c(reciprocity_count = 0.6))  fit <- clogit(event ~ reciprocity_count + strata(stratum), data = cc) coef(fit) #> reciprocity_count  #>             0.542 confint(fit) #>                       2.5 %    97.5 % #> reciprocity_count    0.349     0.734

code: one_run <- function(seed, method, tau = NULL) {   set.seed(seed)   a <- paste0("a", 1:50)   secs <- system.time(     cc <- simulate_relational_events(       n_events = 2000, senders = a, receivers = a, baseline_rate = 1,       endogenous_stats = "reciprocity_binary",       endogenous_effects = c(reciprocity_binary = 0.6),       n_controls = 1, method = method, tau = tau)   )[["elapsed"]]   fit <- clogit(event ~ reciprocity_binary + strata(stratum),                           data = cc)   c(beta = coef(fit)[[1]], seconds = secs) } configs <- list(   "Gillespie"      = list(method = "gillespie", tau = NULL),   "tau-leap 0.01"  = list(method = "tau_leap",  tau = 0.01),   "tau-leap 0.05"  = list(method = "tau_leap",  tau = 0.05),   "tau-leap 0.20"  = list(method = "tau_leap",  tau = 0.20)) runs <- lapply(configs, function(cfg)   t(vapply(1:10, one_run, numeric(2), method = cfg$method, tau = cfg$tau))) tab <- t(vapply(runs, function(r) c(beta_mean = mean(r[, "beta"]),                                     beta_sd   = stats::sd(r[, "beta"]),                                     seconds   = mean(r[, "seconds"])),                 numeric(3))) round(tab, 3) #>               beta_mean beta_sd seconds #> Gillespie         0.563   0.086   0.543 #> tau-leap 0.01     0.636   0.062   0.183 #> tau-leap 0.05     0.585   0.049   0.152 #> tau-leap 0.20     0.587   0.055   0.164 op <- par(mar = c(4, 4.5, 1, 1)) boxplot(lapply(runs, function(r) r[, "beta"]), ylab = expression(hat(beta)),         col = "grey90") abline(h = 0.6, lty = 2, col = "firebrick") par(op)

what: E1 — Recovery of a linear endogenous effect
title: Validation experiments
text: Property. simulator case-control likelihood consistent: true β plugged simulate_relational_events() recovered (Monte Carlo noise) fitting stratified clogit emitted case-control table. Design. Single endogenous term reciprocity_count. 15-actor one-mode network, 800 events per replicate, one control per case. Five target values β ∈ {-0.4, 0, 0.4, 0.8, 1.2} (last deliberate stress row), 30 replicates — 150 fits. Code. Result. Estimates essentially unbiased small moderate β, bias grows effect strength (+0.05 0.8, +0.15 1.2 stress row): high reciprocity events concentrate reciprocating dyads 800-event log becomes informationally limited — real finite-sample effect, bug. Wald coverage sits 0.90 1.00 across cells; β = 0.4 empirical SD (0.086) exceeds mean Wald SE (0.067), interval mildly anticonservative . Two 150 fits emitted clogit convergence warnings (extreme replicates high-β cells); estimates retained.
code: library(amorem) actors <- paste0("a", 1:15); betas <- c(-0.4, 0, 0.4, 0.8, 1.2); n_reps <- 30 res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(betas), function(bi){   b <- betas[bi]; est <- se <- numeric(n_reps)   for (r in 1:n_reps) {     set.seed(20260613L + 1000L*bi + r)     ev <- simulate_relational_events(n_events=800, senders=actors, receivers=actors,             baseline_rate=1, n_controls=1, endogenous_stats="reciprocity_count",             endogenous_effects=c(reciprocity_count=b))     cf <- summary(rem(event~reciprocity_count, data=ev, method="clogit",                       stratum="stratum")$fit)$coefficients     est[r] <- cf[1,"coef"]; se[r] <- cf[1,"se(coef)"]   }   data.frame(beta_true=b, mean_est=mean(est), bias=mean(est)-b, emp_sd=sd(est),              mean_se=mean(se), cov95=mean(est-1.96*se<=b & b<=est+1.96*se)) })) print(round(res, 3), row.names=FALSE) #>  beta_true mean_est   bias emp_sd mean_se cov95 #>       -0.4   -0.395  0.005  0.046   0.043 0.967 #>        0.0   -0.004 -0.004  0.037   0.036 0.933 #>        0.4    0.406  0.006  0.086   0.067 0.900 #>        0.8    0.851  0.051  0.201   0.221 1.000 #>        1.2    1.347  0.147  0.467   0.455 0.967

what: E2 — Recovery of a non-linear smooth effect
title: Validation experiments
text: Property. non-linear dyad-level effect injected via simulator’s contribution_logits matrix recovered, shape, stratified p-spline clogit. Design. Static dyadic covariate x_sr ~ Uniform(0, 6) 18-actor network, true non-linear contribution f(x) = sin(x) − 0.3·(x − 3). simulator runs 1,500 events three controls per case; clogit(event ~ pspline(x, df = 6) + strata(stratum)) extracts partial smooth 150-point grid. Code. Result. Centred RMSE = 0.075, Pearson correlation = 0.998 centred true estimated curves.
code: library(amorem); library(survival)  f_true <- function(x) sin(x) - 0.3 * (x - 3)        # true non-linear effect set.seed(20260518) actors <- paste0("a", 1:18) x_mat  <- matrix(runif(18^2, 0, 6), 18, 18, dimnames = list(actors, actors)) diag(x_mat) <- 0 logit_mat <- f_true(x_mat); diag(logit_mat) <- 0    # static per-dyad log-rate  ev <- simulate_relational_events(   n_events = 1500, senders = actors, receivers = actors,   baseline_rate = 1, n_controls = 3, contribution_logits = logit_mat) ev$x <- mapply(function(s, r) x_mat[s, r], ev$sender, ev$receiver)  # stratified conditional logit with a penalised spline on x fit <- clogit(event ~ pspline(x, df = 6) + strata(stratum), data = ev)  xg <- seq(0.1, 5.9, length.out = 150) nd <- ev[rep(1, length(xg)), ]; nd$x <- xg pr <- predict(fit, newdata = nd, type = "terms", se.fit = TRUE) col <- grep("pspline", colnames(pr$fit), value = TRUE)[1] yy_c     <- pr$fit[, col] - mean(pr$fit[, col])     # centre both curves y_true_c <- f_true(xg)     - mean(f_true(xg)) sqrt(mean((yy_c - y_true_c)^2))   # RMSE cor(yy_c, y_true_c)               # Pearson correlation #> [1] 0.075 #> [1] 0.998

what: E3 — Sender frailty under activity heterogeneity
title: Validation experiments
text: Property tested. data-generating process injects strong per-sender activity heterogeneity, fixed-coefficient clogit reciprocity_count absorb activity gradient slope — Gamma sender frailty correct ? Design. 20-actor network, true reciprocity_count β = 0.5, three controls per case, per-sender baseline offsets injected contribution_logits rows. Two heterogeneity regimes: strong — lognormal activity (median max/min ratio ≈ 84×, “two orders magnitude” redesign experiment previously flagged needed), 2,500 events, 8 replicates; mild — Gamma(2, 1) activity (≈ 22×), 1,500 events, 10 replicates (original design). replicate: naive clogit(event ~ reciprocity_count + strata(stratum)) versus coxph(Surv(rep(1, N), event) ~ reciprocity_count + frailty(sender, "gamma") + strata(stratum)). Code. Result — hypothesized failure mode manifest. naive case-control estimator robust sender-activity heterogeneity: strong regime essentially unbiased (−0.002). Adding Gamma frailty reduce bias either regime — adds small upward bias inflates variance, every frailty fit emitted inner-loop convergence warnings. stratified case-control likelihood already conditions stratum, absorbs per-sender baseline; extra frailty term nothing correct injects noise. revises earlier reading experiment (expected frailty needed called design -powered): stronger design answer correction unnecessary setting.
code: library(amorem); library(survival) B <- 0.5; NA_ <- 20; A <- paste0("a", 1:NA_) run_one <- function(ne, act, seed){ set.seed(seed)   lm <- matrix(log(act), NA_, NA_, dimnames=list(A,A)); diag(lm) <- 0  # sender offsets   ev <- simulate_relational_events(n_events=ne, senders=A, receivers=A, baseline_rate=1,         n_controls=3, contribution_logits=lm,         endogenous_stats="reciprocity_count", endogenous_effects=B)   ev$sender <- factor(ev$sender)   bn <- coef(clogit(event ~ reciprocity_count + strata(stratum), data=ev))[["reciprocity_count"]]   bf <- suppressWarnings(coxph(Surv(rep(1,nrow(ev)),event) ~ reciprocity_count +         frailty(sender,"gamma") + strata(stratum), data=ev)$coefficients[["reciprocity_count"]])   c(bn, bf) } regime <- function(ne, nrep, afun, sb){ m <- t(sapply(1:nrep, function(r){     set.seed(sb+r); a <- afun(NA_); run_one(ne, a, sb+1000+r) }))   cat(sprintf("naive mean=%.3f sd=%.3f bias=%+.3f | frailty mean=%.3f sd=%.3f bias=%+.3f\n",     mean(m[,1]),sd(m[,1]),mean(m[,1])-B, mean(m[,2]),sd(m[,2]),mean(m[,2])-B)) } cat("STRONG (~84x): "); regime(2500, 8, function(n) rlnorm(n,0,1.15), 31000) cat("MILD   (~22x): "); regime(1500,10, function(n) rgamma(n,2,1),   32000) #> STRONG (~84x): naive mean=0.498 sd=0.100 bias=-0.002 | frailty mean=0.539 sd=0.110 bias=+0.039 #> MILD   (~22x): naive mean=0.539 sd=0.086 bias=+0.039 | frailty mean=0.554 sd=0.140 bias=+0.054

title: Validation experiments
text: Property. Gillespie scheme exact per-event; τ-leap scheme bundles events fixed time slices scale better large actor universes. Design. 4 × 5 × 2 grid: n_actors ∈ {15, 30, 60, 100}, n_events ∈ {500, 1000, 2500, 5000, 10000}, method ∈ {gillespie, tau_leap} (τ-leap tau = 0.05). Single endogenous reciprocity term β = 0.4. case-control sampling (n_controls = 0) wall-clock isolates simulator. Timings Apple Silicon (M1 Max) — absolute seconds machine-specific; scaling shape ratios transfer. Code. Result (stable cells). τ-leap 22–42× faster n_actors = 60 37× ≈ 100× faster n_actors = 100, gap widening n_events (Gillespie recomputes full risk set per event; τ-leap takes vectorised Poisson leaps). Failure map (honest). back-ends break small n_actors self-exciting reciprocity process, opposite reasons: Gillespie’s per-dyad softmax underflows (“positive probabilities”) n_actors ∈ {15, 30} n_events ≥ 5000 (60 10,000), τ-leap’s intensities explode memory blow-(seed-dependent small sizes; replicates fail n_events = 10000 n_actors ≤ 60). 10,000 events 100-actor cell clean methods — real limitation worth knowing simulating small, strongly self-exciting networks.
code:
library(amorem) sim_time <- function(na, ne, method, tau=NULL, seed=1) {   act <- paste0("a", seq_len(na)); set.seed(20260613L + seed)   args <- list(n_events=ne, senders=act, receivers=act,     endogenous_stats="reciprocity_count",     endogenous_effects=c(reciprocity_count=0.4),     n_controls=0, method=method)   if (method=="tau_leap") args$tau <- tau   tt <- system.time(r <- tryCatch(do.call(simulate_relational_events, args),                                   error=function(e) e))   if (inherits(r,"error")) return(c(sec=NA, note=conditionMessage(r)))   c(sec=unname(tt[["elapsed"]]), note="ok") } for (ne in c(2500, 10000)) {   g <- as.numeric(sim_time(100, ne, "gillespie")["sec"])   t <- as.numeric(sim_time(100, ne, "tau_leap", tau=0.05)["sec"])   cat(sprintf("na=100 ne=%5d  gil=%.3fs tau=%.3fs  speedup=%.0fx
", ne, g, t, g/t)) } #> na=100 ne= 2500  gil=0.620s tau=0.009s  speedup=~70x #> na=100 ne=10000  gil=3.40s  tau=0.033s  speedup=~100x   (jitters 100-111x) cat("gil na=15 ne=10000:", sim_time(15,10000,"gillespie")["note"], "
") #> gil na=15 ne=10000: too few positive probabilities cat("tau na=15 ne=10000:", sim_time(15,10000,"tau_leap",tau=0.05,seed=2)["note"], "
") #> tau na=15 ne=10000: vector memory limit of 16.0 Gb reached  (divergence)

title: Validation experiments
text: Property. simulator records endogenous statistic fly generates events; post-hoc engine endogenous_features() re-derives statistics timestamps alone. two agree row--row case-control table simulator emits. Design. 15-actor, 1,200-event simulation (one control per case; 2,400-row case-control table) 12 endogenous statistics active simultaneously across five families four variant axes, C++-engine-supported. statistic, compute max |simulator − post-hoc| two recompute conventions: naive recompute full case-control table, aligned recompute passing history_log = realized-event rows (sampled controls neither pollute running history read post-update state tied timestamps). Code. Result — parity holds controls kept history. naive recompute lets sampled control rows write running history (count/exp-decay drift order n_events) lets tied rows read post-update state (timing drift). aligned recompute reproduces simulator’s exact semantics — C++ engine processes rows time groups, every row tied timestamp reads write, event rows write (src/compute_features_cpp.cpp, time-group loop; mask construction R/preprocess.R). alignment engines agree floating-point precision (max 4.3 × 10⁻¹⁴, exp-decay residue summation-order noise). Neither engine needs privileged . naive column experiment gets dropping event column: case-control table keeps , endogenous_features() applies aligned semantics default.
code: library(amorem) set.seed(505) actors <- sprintf("a%02d", 1:15) stats <- c("reciprocity_count","reciprocity_binary","transitivity_count",            "transitivity_binary","transitivity_time_recent","cyclic_count",            "cyclic_exp_decay","cyclic_time_recent","sending_balance_count",            "sending_balance_exp_decay","receiving_balance_count",            "receiving_balance_time_first") stopifnot(all(stats %in% cpp_supported_stats())) ev <- simulate_relational_events(n_events=1200, senders=actors, receivers=actors,         baseline_rate=1, n_controls=1, endogenous_stats=stats,         endogenous_effects=setNames(rep(0,length(stats)),stats), half_life=5) ev$rid <- seq_len(nrow(ev)); base <- ev[,c("rid","sender","receiver","time")] fn <- endogenous_features(base, stats=stats, half_life=5)        # naive hl <- ev[ev$event==1L, c("sender","receiver","time")] fc <- endogenous_features(base, stats=stats, half_life=5,                                   history_log=hl)                        # aligned fn <- fn[order(fn$rid),]; fc <- fc[order(fc$rid),]; evo <- ev[order(ev$rid),] md <- function(a,b){ b[is.na(b)] <- 0; max(abs(a-b)) } cat("naive max:",   max(sapply(stats, function(s) md(evo[[s]], fn[[s]]))),     "| aligned max:", max(sapply(stats, function(s) md(evo[[s]], fc[[s]]))), "\n") #> naive max: 12  | aligned max: 4.263e-14   -> parity holds (all < 1e-9)

what: E6 — Neural backend: gradient correctness and interaction recovery
title: Validation experiments
text: Property. nn backend’s hand-derived analytic gradients must match numerical differentiation, fitted network must () match linear conditional logit truth linear, (b) outperform effects interact way additive model represent. Design. Gradients. 3-feature MLP four strata; compare every analytic gradient entry central finite difference. Recovery. 600 case-1-control strata, event stratum drawn softmax true score. Two regimes: linear truth eta = 1.5*x1 interaction truth eta = 2.5*x1*x2. Fit rem(method = "nn") rem(method = "clogit") compare top-1 concordance (fraction strata whose observed event scores highest). Code. Result — passes. Analytic numerical gradients agree max|analytic - numerical| = 1.4e-10, confirming backprop. linear truth neural backend matches linear conditional logit (0.78 vs 0.78 — overfitting penalty); interaction truth, additive clogit stuck near chance (0.52), joint MLP recovers structure (0.81). learned score surface (right) reproduces saddle 2.5*x1*x2 — high matching-sign corners, low opposite-sign corners. exactly case neural backend : endogenous effects interact, additive backends represent structure, MLP — scores full candidate vector jointly — .
code: library(amorem)  # one event + one control per stratum; the event is drawn by a softmax # over a true score eta(x) make_cc <- function(S, eta, p = 2, seed = 1) {   set.seed(seed); rows <- vector("list", S)   for (s in seq_len(S)) {     X  <- matrix(rnorm(2 * p), 2, p)     pr <- exp(apply(X, 1, eta)); pr <- pr / sum(pr)     e  <- sample(1:2, 1, prob = pr)     d  <- as.data.frame(X); names(d) <- paste0("x", seq_len(p))     d$event <- as.integer(seq_len(2) == e); d$stratum <- s     rows[[s]] <- d[order(-d$event), ]   }   do.call(rbind, rows) } conc <- function(score, strat, event) {            # top-1 concordance   top <- tapply(seq_along(score), strat, function(i) i[which.max(score[i])])   mean(event[as.integer(top)] == 1) }  for (kind in c("linear", "interaction")) {   eta <- if (kind == "linear") function(x) 1.5 * x[1] else function(x) 2.5 * x[1] * x[2]   cc  <- make_cc(600, eta, seed = if (kind == "linear") 2 else 4)   fnn <- rem(event ~ x1 + x2, data = cc, method = "nn",              nn = nn_control(hidden = if (kind == "linear") 8 else c(16, 8),                              epochs = 400, seed = 5))   fcl <- rem(event ~ x1 + x2, data = cc, method = "clogit", stratum = "stratum")   c_cl <- conc(as.matrix(cc[, c("x1", "x2")]) %*% coef(fcl), cc$stratum, cc$event)   cat(kind, "- clogit", round(c_cl, 2), " nn", round(fnn$fit$concordance$all, 2), "\n") } #> linear - clogit 0.78  nn 0.78 #> interaction - clogit 0.52  nn 0.81  # the right panel is the learned score surface: predict(fnn, grid) over x1 x2. # gradient correctness is checked against numerical differentiation in # tests/testthat/test-rem-nn.R (max |analytic - numerical| = 1.4e-10).

what: E7 — Additive-spline (STREAM) backend: recovery, mini-batch invariance, and scaling
title: Validation experiments
text: Property. additive_spline architecture — per-covariate B-spline expansions trained stochastic gradient exact case-control partial likelihood, STREAM construction Filippi-Mazzola & Wit (2024, JRSS-C 73(4)) — must () recover shape additive effects, including returning flat curve null covariate; (b) give fit full-batch mini-batch training; (c) scale better -memory gam backend case-control table grows. Design. Strata one event one control, additive truth eta = sin(2*x1) + 0.8*x2 + 0*x3 (nonlinear, linear, null). Recovery invariance: 2,000 strata, 10 Monte-Carlo replicates, fitting full-batch mini-batched (batch_strata 256 64); fitted f_k report correlation centered truth , null, curve amplitude. Scaling: single fit 2k / 8k / 32k / 64k strata, timing additive-spline SGD (batch_strata = 256) rem(method = "gam") nl() smooths data, recording wall-clock peak R memory. Code. Result — passes three properties. Aggregated 10 replicates: nonlinear linear effects recovered (correlation 0.97–0.99); null effect stays near-flat (amplitude ≈ 0.17 unit-scale signal); fit invariant mini-batching; additive-spline backend beats linear conditional logit concordance (0.74 vs 0.68) captures sin curvature linear fit . left panel overlays fitted curves (solid) truths (dotted). Scaling (single fit per size; wall-clock peak R memory): 64,000 strata additive-spline SGD 1.6× faster uses less memory -memory gam fit, gap widens size — regime STREAM designed , measured modest scale (runs also corroborated second machine; absolute seconds machine-dependent).
code: library(amorem) f1 <- function(x) sin(2*x); f2 <- function(x) 0.8*x          # f3 is the null eta <- function(x) f1(x[1]) + f2(x[2]) + 0*x[3] make_cc <- function(S, seed) { set.seed(seed); rows <- vector("list", S)   for (s in seq_len(S)) { X <- matrix(rnorm(6), 2, 3)     pr <- exp(apply(X, 1, eta)); pr <- pr/sum(pr); e <- sample(1:2, 1, prob = pr)     d <- as.data.frame(X); names(d) <- c("x1","x2","x3")     d$event <- as.integer(seq_len(2) == e); d$stratum <- s     rows[[s]] <- d[order(-d$event), ] }   do.call(rbind, rows) }  cc  <- make_cc(2000, seed = 7101) fit <- rem(event ~ x1 + x2 + x3, data = cc, method = "nn",            nn = nn_control(architecture = "additive_spline", spline_df = 8,                            batch_strata = 256, epochs = 80, lr = 5e-2, seed = 7201))  g  <- seq(-2, 2, length.out = 81)                  # read each fitted f_k off a grid f1_hat <- predict(fit, data.frame(x1 = g, x2 = 0, x3 = 0)) cor(f1_hat - mean(f1_hat), f1(g) - mean(f1(g)))     # ~ 0.98 vs the sin truth #> [1] 0.978

title: Augmented Modelling of Relational Events
text: amorem — end--end simulation, sampling, feature engineering, model selection, inference relational event models (REMs) R, one consistent API. package consolidates four lines recent methodological work: Dyadic REMs timing / closure variants one- two-axis actor frailty, following Juozaitienė & Wit (2024, JRSS-). Relational Hyper Event Models (RHEMs) set-valued sender/receiver hyperedges, subset-repetition covariates, smooth effects (linear / tv / nl / tvnl), following Boschi, Lerner & Wit (2025). Global covariate effects — covariates varying time constant across pairs — via time-shifted partial likelihood Lembo, Juozaitienė, Vinciotti & Wit (2025, JRSS-C). Cumulative martingale-residual GOF tests, following Boschi & Wit (2025, Stat & Comp 36:4).

title: Augmented Modelling of Relational Events
text: rem() — unified fitter preprocessed case-control data, conditional-logit backend (case-k-control) gam backend (case-1-control) supporting linear / tv / nl / tvnl smooth effects re() random effects, plus summary() / coef() / plot(). widen_case_control() reshapes long case-control log wide form rem() expects. simulate_relational_events() — exact Gillespie τ-leap; composes exogenous, endogenous, time-varying global covariates; wide = TRUE emits ready--fit case-1-control table. endogenous_features() — endogenous catalogue computed post-hoc (sender, receiver, time) log. case-control data observed events build network history; sampled controls scored without entering . sample_non_events() — nested case-control sampling appearance / citation / remove risk-set rules, time-shifted sampling (shift = "exponential") keeps global covariates estimable. Datasets — event logs published interaction networks, enso_nino34, reconstructed El Niño index (1301–2005) use global covariate. Goodness fit — gof_rem() tests fitted rem() model (time, functional-form score processes, bootstrap null accounts estimated coefficients); gof_univariate(), gof_multivariate(), gof_global(), gof_auxiliary() refit linear model event log; pointwise martingale_residuals(). earlier compare_models(), compare_models_smooth() compare_models_global() remain available (superseded rem()).

what: Compare REM specifications with global covariate effects — compare_models_global
title: Compare REM specifications with global covariate effects — compare_models_global
text:
Superseded rem(), unified front-end fitting relational event models preprocessed case-control data. compare_models_global() remains fully supported. Implements time-shifted partial likelihood Lembo, Juozaitienė, Vinciotti & Wit (2025) fitting relational event models global covariate effects — covariates time-dependent constant across interacting pairs (e.g.\ temperature, time day, residual baseline hazard). Standard case-control partial likelihood identify global terms cancel rate ratio; function follows paper's Section 4 recipe: random per-dyad time shift breaks cancellation, one non-event per event partial likelihood reduces degenerate logistic additive model fit mgcv::gam(). Per paper's equations 11-13: $$   \mathcal{L}^{PS}(f, g) = \prod_{k=1}^n      rac{\exp\{\Delta_k(f; x_{s_k r_k}) + \Delta_k(g; x_k)\}}          {1 + \exp\{\Delta_k(f; x_{s_k r_k}) + \Delta_k(g; x_k)\}} $$ \(\Delta_k\) difference (smooth) function evaluated focal event time sampled non-event's back-shifted time \(t^*_k = t_k + h_{s_k r_k} - h_{s^* r^*}\). Shift distribution. case-control sample drawn sample_non_events() shift = "exponential": one shift per dyad, \(H_{sr} \sim \mathrm{Exp}\) mean \(
u\) times average event time (measured start window), control drawn dyads whose back-shifted time lies window, events dyad dropped. Dyadic statistics control computed events time \(t^*_k\). paper uses \(
u = 1\) reports effect \(
u\) estimates \(
u \[0.1, 100]\). Specification format. entry models named character vector mapping covariate name (statistic endogenous_features() column global_covariates) effect type: "linear" – linear beta * x term. "nl"     – smooth s(x) (thin-plate, paper's default). "tv"     – smooth s(time, = x) (time-varying). "tvnl"   – tensor product te(time, x). "global_smooth" – smooth s(x_global) evaluated focal time vs. non-event's shifted time (paper's g_b(x^{(b)}(t)) family). "global_cyclic" – cyclic smooth s(x_global, bs = "cc") time--day-like covariates periodic domain. "global_time" – smooth time , recovering residual time effect \(g_0(t)\) paper eq. 3.

what: Compare candidate specifications with smooth (TV / NL / TVNL) effects — compare_models_smooth
title: Compare candidate specifications with smooth (TV / NL / TVNL) effects — compare_models_smooth
text: Superseded rem(), fits smooth (TV / NL / TVNL) effects preprocessed case-control data. compare_models_smooth() remains fully supported. Mirrors compare_models() lets statistic specification take one four effect types instead single linear coefficient: linear, time-varying (TV), non-linear (NL), jointly time-varying non-linear (TVNL). smooth machinery follows Boschi, Lerner & Wit (2025); matrix--event-vs-non-event trick documented Section 3.3. specification: One case-control sample drawn event_log n_controls = 1 (paired event / non-event design). every requested statistic, case (event) control (non-event) features computed via endogenous_features(). mgcv design uses case-vs-control matrix trick: linear -> single coefficient case - control (column d_stat). tv    -> s(time, = d_stat) — smooth time, multiplied d_stat. nl    -> s(stat_mat, = I_mat) stat_mat two-column matrix cbind(case, control) I_mat cbind(1, -1). tvnl  -> te(time_mat, stat_mat, = I_mat) tensor product smooth, time_mat columns equal event time vector. model fitted mgcv::gam degenerate logistic likelihood: response = rep(1, n), formula = one ~ -1 + ..., family = binomial. matches Boschi et al. equation 8. AIC values directly comparable across specifications every fit uses case-control sample. Returns tidy data.frame compare_models().

text: event_log data.frame containing least sender, receiver, time columns. stats Character vector statistics compute.  See Details full list allowed values. half_life Positive numeric; half-life parameter \(T\) exponential-decay statistics (*_exp_decay*). sort Logical; TRUE, events ordered time prior computing summaries (ties preserve input order). history_log Optional data.frame giving authoritative event history (columns sender, receiver, time). supplied, rows event_log whose (sender, receiver, time) triple appears history_log update running network state; rows (e.g. sampled non-events / controls) statistics computed history never enter . makes possible evaluate endogenous statistics non-events without non-events polluting history. NULL (default) event_log case-control data – 0/1 event column control rows, written sample_non_events() – event == 1 rows update history; otherwise every row treated event. Pass history_log = event_log treat every row event regardless. prior_log Optional data.frame events precede study window (columns sender, receiver, time), used warm-start network state. rows always update running state never appear returned data.frame. separates warm-starting non-event masking role history_log: pass earlier history prior_log use history_log purely mark rows event_log real events. title: Compute endogenous event-network statistics — endogenous_features
text: event log added columns, one per requested statistic (sender_receivers_set added list-column).

title: Compute endogenous event-network statistics — endogenous_features
text: statistics evaluated immediately event logged.  grouped five families. Degree / baseline: sender_outdegree Number events previously sent sender. receiver_indegree Number events previously received receiver. recency Elapsed time since last event ordered pair; NA dyad brand new. Reciprocity — reverse-dyad (receiver \(\\) sender) history: reciprocity / reciprocity_binary 1 reverse dyad ever observed, 0 otherwise. reciprocity_count Total count past reverse-dyad events. reciprocity_exp_decay Exponentially weighted sum past reverse-dyad events (requires half_life). reciprocity_time_recent Elapsed time since recent reverse-dyad event; NA none. reciprocity_time_first Elapsed time since first reverse-dyad event; NA none. Transitivity — two-path \(s \k \r\): transitivity_binary 1 intermediary \(k\) exists \((s,k)\) \((k,r)\) \(t\). transitivity_count Number intermediaries. transitivity_binary_ordered Like binary requiring \((s,k)\) precede \((k,r)\). transitivity_count_ordered Count order restriction. transitivity_exp_decay Exp-decay weighted sum two-paths (requires half_life). transitivity_exp_decay_ordered Exp-decay order restriction. transitivity_time_recent Time since recently completed two-path; NA none. transitivity_time_first Time since earliest two-path; NA none. transitivity_time_recent_ordered Time since recent ordered two-path; NA none. transitivity_time_first_ordered Time since earliest ordered two-path; NA none. Cyclic closure — two-path \(r \k \s\), closed \(s \r\): cyclic_binary 1 cyclic two-path exists. cyclic_count Number cyclic intermediaries. cyclic_time_recent Time since recent cyclic two-path formation; NA none. cyclic_time_first Time since first cyclic two-path formation; NA none. Sending balance — shared target: \(s \k\) \(r \k\) exist: sending_balance_binary 1 shared target exists. sending_balance_count Number shared targets. sending_balance_time_recent Time since recent shared-target two-path formation; NA none. sending_balance_time_first Time since first shared-target two-path formation; NA none. Receiving balance — shared source: \(k \s\) \(k \r\) exist: receiving_balance_binary 1 shared source exists. receiving_balance_count Number shared sources. receiving_balance_time_recent Time since recent shared-source two-path formation; NA none. receiving_balance_time_first Time since first shared-source two-path formation; NA none. statistic "sender_receivers_set" special: adds list-column element character vector receivers row's sender reached row (building block set-valued endogenous covariates, e.g. alien species' previously invaded regions). honours history_log, can computed sampled non-events without non-events polluting history.

text: Two estimation backends provided: "gam" Degenerate logistic regression case-1-control design (Boschi, Lerner & Wit 2025): response constant 1 linear predictor built event-minus-control differences. "clogit" Conditional logistic regression case-k-control design via survival::clogit() (linear terms ). case/control strata taken stratum, derived cumsum(case == 1) stratum NULL (assuming case immediately followed controls, eventnet blocked layout). Two architectures via nn_control(): multilayer perceptron scoring full covariate vector jointly (interaction-capable), additive_spline predictor — per-covariate B-spline expansions fitted stochastic gradient, STREAM construction Filippi-Mazzola & Wit (2024, JRSS-C). coefficient table; summary() reports -sample (, validation split, held-) concordance plot(type = "pdp") shows per-feature curves. title: Sample non-events for inference — sample_non_events
text:
event_log Data frame columns sender, receiver, time. n_controls Number non-events (controls) sample per realized event. scope Candidate set definition. "" uses every actor observed data; "appearance" restricts actors appeared prior events (first event, prior events, gets controls); "citation" matches citation networks senders restricted papers debut current time receivers must appeared earlier; always draws senders receivers two separate pools, whatever mode says. mode "one" (default) draws sender receiver candidate pool (single-mode): every actor seen either role can control sender receiver, networks whose senders receivers one node set (e.g. bike stations, e-mail users). "two" samples sender receiver separate pools (two-mode): actor seen receiver never control sender, vice versa, bipartite networks (e.g. species invading regions). risk Strategy governing risk set. "standard" (default) keeps unrealized dyads available across strata, whereas "remove" deletes dyad candidate pool occurred (useful processes species invasions pair reoccur). "remove", dyads firing focal event's timestamp also kept control pool (concurrent events valid non-events instant). exclude_pairs Optional two-column data.frame/matrix (sender, receiver) pairs structurally ineligible controls must never sampled (e.g. alien species' native range, dyad forbidden advance). Columns named sender/receiver used present, otherwise first two columns. exclude_concurrent Logical; keep dyads event focal event's timestamp control pool? Defaults TRUE risk = "remove" FALSE risk = "standard", tied event still risk instant (Breslow convention). allow_loops Logical; can sampled non-events identical sender receiver? seed Optional seed reproducibility. max_attempts Maximum resampling attempts per control giving (prevents infinite loops candidate sets small). shift = "exponential" number rejection draws tried valid candidates enumerated, sampling never fails . shift "none" (default) gives every control event's time, global covariate (function time , e.g. weather time day) takes value within stratum cancels partial likelihood. "exponential" samples controls time-shifted copy event process (Lembo, Juozaitienė, Vinciotti & Wit 2025, Section 4), controls carry times global effects stay estimable; see Time-shifted sampling. shift_scale Positive number \(
u\): shifts mean \(
u\) times average event time, measured start window (paper uses \(
u = 1\)). Larger shifts carry information global effects, leave events control. Used shift = "exponential". window Observation window c(start, end) shift = "exponential". Defaults c(min(time), max(time)); pass true window (paper's \([0, T]\)) known.

title: Sample non-events for inference — sample_non_events
text: shift = "exponential", every dyad risk set (sender \(\times\) receiver pairs mode = "two", ordered actor pairs mode = "one") draws one shift \(h_{sr} \sim \mathrm{Exp}\), reused every event dyad. Event \(k\) dyad \((s, r)\) moves \(t^e = t_k + h_{sr}\); control drawn uniformly dyads whose back-shifted time \(t^* = t^e - h_{s^*r^*}\) lies window, stored time \(t^*\). risk-set rules evaluated \(t^*\): exclude_pairs always applies; risk = "remove" dyad fired \(t^*\) risk; scope = "appearance" actors must appeared event \(t^*\). event whose shifted risk set holds valid dyad carries information gets controls. scope = "citation" supported, exclude_concurrent used (control times continuous). Covariates control must evaluated time: compute endogenous statistics endogenous_features(cc, stats, history_log = event_log), evaluates row events strictly , evaluate global covariates row's time. widen_case_control() gives time_ev / time_nv <cov>_ev / <cov>_nv, global effect fitted rem(~ nl(<cov>)), baseline rem(~ nl(time)).

title: Simulate relational event sequences — simulate_relational_events
text: n_events Number events generate. senders Character vector listing sender set \(\mathcal{S}\). receivers Character vector listing receiver set \(\mathcal{R}\). baseline_rate Positive scalar. constant baseline hazard multiplier applied dyads. Defaults 1. start_time Initial time stamp. horizon Optional maximum horizon; simulation stops cumulative time exceed value. contribution_logits Optional length(senders) x length(receivers) matrix dyad-level contributions log-rate (.e. dyad-specific part linear predictor, distinct baseline hazard). Defaults zeros. sender_covariates Optional numeric data.frame/matrix one row per sender. sender_effects Optional numeric vector coefficients sender_covariates. Required sender covariates supplied. receiver_covariates Optional numeric data.frame/matrix one row per receiver. receiver_effects Optional numeric vector coefficients receiver_covariates. Required receiver covariates supplied. allow_loops Logical; whether sender receiver can coincide. n_controls Integer; number non-events (controls) sample uniformly random realized event. n_controls > 0, function returns case-control data frame suitable conditional logistic regression / GAM modeling. Defaults 0. endogenous_stats Optional character vector endogenous mechanisms include rate. entry updates state matrix every event intensity next event depends realized history. Supported values: "reciprocity_count" — number past reverse-dyad events. "reciprocity_binary" — 1 reverse dyad fired least , 0 otherwise. "reciprocity_exp_decay" — sum past reverse-dyad events exponential half-life decay (requires half_life). "transitivity_exp_decay" — \(\sum_{k} e^{-(t - t^{(s,k,r)}_{\text{form}}) \log 2 / T}\) \(t^{(s,k,r)}_{\text{form}}\) formation time two-path \(s \k \r\) (definition \(t^{(5c)}\) Juozaitienė & Wit, 2024). Requires half_life. "transitivity_exp_decay_ordered" — "transitivity_exp_decay" counts ordered two-paths (s → k strictly k → r), definition \(t^{(6c)}\).  Requires half_life. "cyclic_exp_decay" — exp-decayed sum cyclic two-paths \(r \k \s\) (paper \(c^{(5c)}\)).  Requires half_life. "sending_balance_exp_decay" — exp-decayed sum shared-target two-paths \(s \k,\ r \k\) (paper \(sb^{(5c)}\)).  Requires half_life. title: Recency transform of inter-event time gaps — transform_recency
text: Maps non-negative time gaps \(\delta\) bounded recency weights via $$   w(\delta) \;=\; \exp\!\Bigl(-\frac{\delta}{2\,m}\Bigr), $$ \(m\) median supplied (reference) gaps. text: CRAN release: 2026-06-29 First CRAN release, name amorem. package renamed working name amore, collided (case-insensitively) archived CRAN package AMORE. release consolidates 0.9.0 development line first stable, installable version: unified rem() front-end (clogit, gam, nn backends, including additive-spline architecture), Gillespie / tau-leap simulation engine, endogenous-statistics catalogue, martingale-residual goodness--fit family. Relative 0.9.0 package renamed amorem exported feature functions dropped compute_ prefix — compute_endogenous_features() compute_hyperedge_features() became endogenous_features() hyperedge_features(); rest API unchanged.

title: amorem 1.0.0
text: torch training engine rem(method = "nn"). nn_control(engine = "torch") trains model conditional-logistic loss built-pure-R engine using torch (libtorch autograd + Adam), markedly faster , batch_strata, scaling large event logs (optionally GPU). fitted object interchangeable R engine. torch Suggests dependency; torch engine requires equal-sized strata. nn_uncertainty() quantifies uncertainty neural fit stratum bootstrap, returning partial-dependence uncertainty bands concordance confidence interval (print() plot() methods) — inferential counterpart point-prediction nn backend otherwise lacks.

title: amorem 0.9.0
text: New neural backend small number API refinements; version intended first CRAN release. STREAM-style additive splines: nn_control(architecture = "additive_spline", batch_strata = ) fits per-covariate B-spline effects (mini-batch) stochastic gradient exact case-control partial likelihood — construction Filippi-Mazzola & Wit (2024, JRSS-C, doi:10.1093/jrsssc/qlae023) — giving interpretable additive smooth curves objective clogit, mini-batching large event logs. New rem(method = "nn") backend: multilayer perceptron scores every candidate case-control stratum trained conditional-logistic partial likelihood (softmax risk set) — nonlinear, prediction-oriented counterpart clogit. Pure-R implementation (extra dependencies), configured via nn_control(); summary() reports -sample (, validation split, held-) concordance plot(type = "pdp") shows per-feature partial-dependence curves. API: degenerate-logistic backend now method = "gam" ("degenerate"); smooth-term wrappers tv() / nl() / tvnl() (tve() / nle() / tvnle()); re() unchanged. rem()’s case argument now defaults NULL taken formula’s left-hand side (e.g. event ~ x) clogit/nn backends. widen_case_control() auto-detects 0/1 indicator column (event IS_OBSERVED) case given. widen_case_control() now carries sender/receiver identifiers case matched control output (sender_ev/receiver_ev/ sender_nv/receiver_nv); new keep_ids argument controls (default TRUE). dyads behind pair longer lost, re() grouping terms can reach actor levels (#92). rem(method = "gam") now detects long-format case-control input (event/IS_OBSERVED indicator control rows) widens widen_case_control() fitting, emitting message — instead silently misreading raw per-row values event-minus-control differences (#93). compute_endogenous_features() gains prior_log argument warm-starting network state events precede study window: rows update running state never appear output, separating warm-starting non-event masking role history_log (#94). cpp_supported_stats() now exported.

title: amorem 0.1.0
text: First release. rem() unified fitter preprocessed case-control data, gam (case-1-control logistic via mgcv::gam()) clogit backend. Smooth-term formula wrappers gam backend (time-varying, non-linear, time-varying-non-linear) re() grouping random effect; re() reproduces Intro--REM tutorial parameterization, rem() exposes gam_method argument. Simulation via simulate_relational_events() (Gillespie tau-leap), endogenous-statistic feature engine, non-event sampling, martingale-residual goodness--fit family.
